nodes.label: Cached AI expense summaries, one row per tenant per scope (overall/business/vehicle)
Rationale: the summary is cached so the portal renders it instantly on revisit instead of re-running the LLM
Read-for-tenant / write-for-service_role split on the expense summary cache
Cached summary records the row count and total it was generated from, so staleness is detectable
Trax Pricing: cross-tenant comparable-based rental price suggestion
Three-tier comparable ladder with minimum samples: make+model+year+/-3 (high, n>=3), make+model (medium, n>=3), make only (low, n>=5)
Rationale: only medians, percentiles and counts leave the function, never another tenant's individual vehicle rows
SECURITY DEFINER function with an explicit caller-owns-vehicle-or-super-admin check as its tenant boundary
Draft mode prices a vehicle that has no row yet, from typed make/model/year, with no utilisation factor
90-day utilisation nudges the price off the comp median toward p75 (high use) or p25 (low use)
Rationale: the SQL does math only; the friendly 'Why?' narrative is generated separately by an LLM
Below the sample thresholds the function returns confidence 'none' rather than a weak guess
Super-admin bypass added to the expense-receipts storage upload policy
Gotcha: super admins have tenant_id NULL, so a folder-prefix storage policy built on get_user_tenant_id() silently rejects their uploads
Atomic mid-rental vehicle swap RPC
Rationale: reassigning the vehicle in place avoids closing and recreating the rental
Rationale: rental, both vehicle statuses, the maintenance block and the history row must move together, so it is one RPC
Swap preconditions: same-tenant replacement, rental not finished, not the same car, not a disposed car
Rationale: double-booking protection is delegated to the existing prevent_rental_overlap trigger instead of re-checked in the RPC
Old vehicle returns to Available only when no other Active/Pending rental still holds it
Swap history row recording old/new vehicle, reason and the acting staff user
Tenants may read swap history, but writes only through the SECURITY DEFINER RPC or service_role
Swapped-out vehicle reads 'Maintenance' rather than 'Available' while its block window is live
Daily 01:00 UTC pg_cron sweep returning vehicles from Maintenance to Rented/Available once no block covers today
Rationale: a maintenance window ending is a pure clock event with no row change, so only a scheduled sweep can clear the status
Coupling: this migration CREATE OR REPLACEs the entire swap RPC, so the two vehicle-swap migrations must be read and edited together
upfront_monthly plan billing model: card taken at a hard gate, first charge one calendar month later
Rationale: upfront_monthly rides Stripe's trial primitive mechanically but is never presented to the customer as a free trial
Auto-extension cron jobs repointed at a hardcoded project URL
Gotcha: current_setting('app.settings.supabase_url') is unset on this database, so both jobs raised before net.http_post and auto-extend rentals silently stopped renewing and charging for days
Rationale: both target functions are verify_jwt=false, so the cron posts with only a Content-Type header
Jobs altered by jobname so the fix does not depend on pg_cron job ids
Distance-banded delivery fees for area delivery mode
Rationale: bands stored canonically in kilometres to match pickup_area_radius_km / return_area_radius_km even though operators quote miles
Resolver picks the first band where distance <= up_to_km; a trailing null band is open-ended, otherwise the address is out of range
Rationale: with delivery_tiers_enabled false the existing flat area_delivery_fee still applies, so the change is behaviour-neutral
Per-vehicle pickup-location assignment so booking offers only the cars at the chosen pickup point
Rationale: NULL means 'available from any location', so every existing vehicle is unchanged until an operator assigns one
Rationale: ON DELETE SET NULL reverts vehicles to any-location instead of blocking deletion of a pickup location
Company name and registration on the customer so a business renter is captured once and reused on later rentals
Global super-admin kill-switch hiding the subscription/setup blocker for every tenant
Rationale: the kill-switch only hides the blocking dialog; subscription status, plans and billing are untouched
Optional hard cap in km on how far an operator will deliver
Gotcha (Open Bay / Jim): the open-ended 'anywhere further' tier band has no ceiling, so a customer far from the service centre still gets a quote
Per-tenant override suppressing the subscription/setup blocker for one tenant
Tenant override is OR-combined with the global admin_settings kill-switch and read through TenantContext
Gotcha: two unrelated migrations share the 20260618140000 timestamp (delivery max distance and the tenant gate override), so their order is filename-alphabetical
rental_additional_drivers added to the supabase_realtime publication
Gotcha: the additional-drivers card subscribed to realtime but the table was never published, so verification/signing badges only refreshed on page load
A2P 10DLC SMS opt-in consent stored on the phone owner and on the booking
Gotcha: the booking form's SMS consent checkbox was collected but never persisted, leaving no proof of opt-in that A2P 10DLC requires
Rationale: the rental carries a point-in-time consent snapshot so the proof is tied to the specific booking
Consent is set true when the box is ticked and never auto-revoked
Duration-based promo codes that auto-apply to fixed rentals lasting at least N days
Highest qualifying duration tier wins when several codes match the rental length
Rationale: auto-apply is deliberately excluded from installment plans, PAYG and auto-extend renewal cycles
Promotions merged into promo codes: each code carries its own marketing card and public-page flag
Backfill keeps duration codes advertised on the public promotions page after the merge
Promo-code uniqueness rescoped from global to per-tenant
Gotcha: a global UNIQUE(code) let one tenant's OFF20 block every other tenant, surfacing as a duplicate-key error on a code the operator did not have
Server-side persistence of in-progress Bonzah onboarding form state, one draft per tenant
Rationale: the draft previously lived only in browser localStorage and was lost on device switch or cache clear
The form upserts the whole draft JSONB on every change and the row is cleared on final submission
Promotions decoupled from promo codes again; the marketing columns are dropped three days after being added
Rationale: Promotions is operator-authored CMS advertising in the promotions table; promo codes are not advertised there
min_duration_days is deliberately retained, so duration auto-discounts survive the revert
Consequence: the DROP discards any marketing copy and banner URLs operators authored during the three-day merge window
payment_model: legacy platform-created Express account versus operator-owned Standard account connected by OAuth
UK to UAE platform migration: which platform Stripe account bills each tenant's SaaS subscription
platform_account stamped on payments and rentals so in-flight money objects keep using the keys they were created with
Rationale: without per-record stamping, captures, refunds and deposit ops on in-flight records break the moment a tenant is flipped to the new platform
Stripe price and subscription objects are account-specific, so plans and subscriptions record their platform account
Per-tenant toggle hiding the gig-driver self-identify checkbox on the booking page
Optional day-of-week schedule for auto-extension payment reminders (Kristen / RevTek request)
Weekday evaluated in the tenant's local timezone, at most once that day, still capped by auto_extend_reminder_max
Rationale: NULL preserves the interval-based cadence so no existing rental changes until a weekday is picked
Per-day versus per-trip billing for rental extras (Open Bay / Jim request)
Rationale: billing_type (how often it is charged) is a new axis orthogonal to pricing_type (where the price comes from)
billing_type snapshotted on the booking selection so historical totals survive later catalog edits
Per-tenant go-live anchor date for the first upfront_monthly platform charge
Gotcha: the first charge was hardcoded to one month from whenever the operator clicked Complete Setup, wrong when the card is entered days or weeks after going live
Month 1 is collected outside the platform during the sales call, so the platform's first charge is really month 2
